symptom: Commands run against the new build wrote into ~/.hermes, the old estate.
root_cause: hermes_constants.py:59 defaults HERMES_HOME to Path.home()/'.hermes'. Any bare `hermes` call in the new tree silently used the old home.
class: Any tool whose target is an environment variable with a default will hit the default the one time nobody sets it.

lesson.statement: Never call a tool that takes its target from the environment without a wrapper that sets the target.

symptom: The new build's worktree contained 10966 files from the old estate.
root_cause: A worktree of an existing branch carries that branch's tree. 'New branch' was read as 'new work', not 'empty tree'.
class: Any branch created off a populated history starts populated, so 'start clean' needs an explicit emptying step.

lesson.statement: When the instruction is start from nothing, prove the tree is empty before the first commit.

root_cause: Unknown. Not yet investigated. The app answers, so it is running; the path is not documented anywhere in the repo.
class: Any service whose health path is not written down will be reported down by the next thing that probes it.

lesson.statement: A service with no recorded health path is an open question, not an incident. Ask once, record the answer.

symptom: The first WATCH run died: HTTP 402 from OpenRouter, 'requires more credits'. Requested 64000 tokens, could afford 1239.
root_cause: OPENAI_BASE_URL points at OpenRouter and the model string 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5' routed there. The OpenRouter account has no credit. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was present and working the whole time.
class: Any estate configured with two providers will use the wrong one the moment nobody names which.

lesson.statement: Name the provider explicitly in config, at every level. A model string that implies a provider is not a choice, it is a default.

symptom: The monitor reported 'Platform: serving, 200'. The 200 was a login page. /health returns 307 to /login?next=%2Fhealth and curl -L follows it.
root_cause: The probe followed redirects. Behind a login, every path answers 200 once you follow, so the check could never fail no matter what the app did.
class: Any health check that follows redirects measures the redirect target, not the service.

lesson.statement: Probe with no-follow and decide health from the code the service itself returned. Following a redirect turns a monitor into a formality.

symptom: I nearly held up a destroy on a '17-row gap' between 3,608 Postgres rows and 3,591 dossier files. There was no gap. A peer pointed out I was comparing rows to files, which are different objects. The sqlite table held exactly 3,608.
class: Two counts of different things are not a comparison, however close they land. Near-equality is the trap: it looks like a small discrepancy instead of a category error.

lesson.statement: Before comparing two counts, say what one unit is on each side. If the units differ, the comparison is void, not close.

guard: A peer with the other half of the estate. The check cost one message and one query.

symptom: The build had a README, an installer and a green bin/verify, and could not be installed. Cloning it into an empty directory and running ./install died three times: .env.example was caught by the .gitignore rule '.env.*' so it never reached a clone; the installer demanded an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY that this estate does not have and never had, because it runs on a Claude Code OAuth login; and the prerequisite check enforced a python floor but no ceiling, so it accepted 3.14.6 and pip then refused it.
class: Verifying in the directory where it was built. Every check passed against a working tree that already had the files, the credentials and the interpreter, none of which a new machine has. The install path was the one path never exercised.

lesson.statement: A setup is not proven by running its verifier in place. Clone into an empty directory, install a different estate, and run it there. Nothing else finds these.
lesson.artifact: REQUIREMENTS.jsonl REQ-123 (a clone holds every file install reads) and bin/verify's python-bound comparison

guard: REQ-123 fails if any file install reads is untracked. bin/verify fails if install's python bound drifts from the agent's requires-python line.

symptom: Installing a second estate ('acme') from a clean clone reached step 5 and stopped: "render: estate.yaml has no value for '{{ service.engine.app }}'". Nine templates addressed services by the first estate's own keys - engine, store-web, store-api - about 45 references. Every one of them rendered perfectly for the estate they were written in.
class: A template that names its own estate is indistinguishable from a correct template until a second estate exists. The template language offered per-key addressing, so the first estate used it, and nothing could tell the difference.

lesson.statement: Take the capability away rather than document not using it. render now exits on any {{ service.<key>.<field> }} and templates loop with {{#services}} instead, so the estate-specific version cannot be written at all.
lesson.artifact: bin/render one_value() refuses paths starting 'service.'; REQUIREMENTS.jsonl REQ-131

guard: bin/render exits 1 naming the offending placeholder and the loop to use instead. render --check runs inside bin/verify, so a template that names one service fails the install.

symptom: bin/verify printed "PASS the gateway is running - jobs fire on schedule" on an estate where no gateway had ever been started and no cron job existed. The check ran `hermes cron list` and looked for the string "Gateway is not running"; with zero jobs installed that command prints no warning at all, so the check read silence as health.
class: Proving a positive by the absence of a negative. The instrument only knows how to see the bad case, so every state it was not built for - including the empty one - comes back green.

lesson.statement: Ask the thing itself and match the positive string. `hermes cron status` says whether the ticker is alive, which is the question; a gateway process that exists with a stalled ticker is now a FAIL rather than a PASS.
lesson.artifact: bin/verify check 10 matches "cron jobs will fire automatically" and has a separate STALLED branch

guard: bin/verify fails on a stalled ticker and reports IDLE when nothing is running. Proven on a clean estate with no gateway (IDLE) and by the string the agent actually emits, hermes_cli/cron.py:344.
